questions.q: The maximum vertical height to which a man can throw a ball is $136m$. The maximum horizontal distance upto which he can throw the same ball is
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Maximum height is achieved when the projection is along the vertical direction,

${H}_\max = \dfrac{v2}{2g} = 136m$

Now, for maximum range, angle of projection should be~$45 °$. Therefore,

${R}_\max = \dfrac{v2}{g} = 2{H}_\max$

$= 2 \left(136\right)$

$= 272m

$

$
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
$m{ω}^{2}acos\theta = mgsin\theta$

$\omega = \sqrt{\dfrac{gtan\theta}{a}}$

$y = 4cx^{2}$

$tan\theta = \dfrac{dy}{dx} = 8xC$

$( tan\theta{)}_{a, b} = 8aC$

$\omega = \sqrt{\dfrac{g \times 8ac}{a}} = 2\sqrt{2gC}$

questions.q: A bomb is dropped by a fighter plane flying horizontally. To an observer sitting in the plane, the trajectory of the bomb is a :
options: straight line vertically down the plane
parabola in a direction opposite to the motion of plane
parabola in the direction of motion of plane
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution: The bomb after being dropped from the plane will have only horizontal velocity but zero vertical velocity. This scenario is as same as if a body is horizontally projected from the top of a tower, and it hits the ground tracing a parabolic path. Hence, the trajectory of the bomb is also a parabola, in the direction of motion of the plane. But if we look the trajectory with respect to observer sitting in the plane then this looks like straight line vertically down the plane due to same horizontal velocity.

questions.q: The distance of the Sun from earth is $1 . 5 \times {10}^{11}m$ and its angular diameter is $2000 ''$ when observed from the earth. The diameter of the Sun will be
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Diameter of Sun is& $D = r\theta$

= 1.5 $\times {10}^{11} \times ($2000 ) $\times \left(\dfrac{1}{3600}\right) \times\left(\dfrac{#960;}${180}\right)$
= 1.45 $\times {10}^{9}$m

$

questions.q: A child of mass $5$ kg is going round a merry-go-round that makes $1$ rotation in $3 . 14s$. The radius of the merry-go-round is~$2m$. The centrifugal force on the child will be
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
The angular speed& \left(\omega\right)$~of the child can be calculated as follows:

$\begin{cases}\omega & = & \dfrac{2\pi}{3 . 14} \\ = & 2rads^{- 1}\end{cases}$

The formula to calculate the centrifugal force on the child is given by

${F}_{r} = m{ω}^{2}r . . . ( 1 )$

Substitute the values of the known parameters into equation (1) to calculate the required centrifugal force.

$\begin{cases}{F}_{r} & = & 5kg \times \left(2rads^{- 1}\right)2 \times 2m \\ = & 40N\end{cases}$

$

questions.q: A shell is fired from a fixed artillery gun with an initial speed u such that it hits the target on the ground at a distance $R$ from it. If ${t}_{1}$ and ${t}_{2}$ are the values of the time taken by it to hit the target in two possible ways, the product ${t}_{1}{t}_{2}$ is:
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
We know for complementary angle range is same for same projection speed.
${t}_{1} = \dfrac{2usin ( \theta )}{g}$ ….. (i)
${t}_{2} = \dfrac{2usin ( 90 - \theta )}{g}$ ….. (ii)
$R = \dfrac{2u^{2}sin \theta cos\theta}{g}$ .… (iii)
From equation (i) and (ii)
${t}_{1}{t}_{2} = \dfrac{4U^{2}sin\theta cos\theta}{g^{2}}$
(Using the value of R from equation iii)
${t}_{1}{t}_{2} = \dfrac{2R}{g}$

questions.q: A particle is moving with constant speed in a circular path. When the particle turns by an angle $90 ° ,$ the ratio of instantaneous velocity to its~average velocity is $\pi: x\sqrt{2} .$~The~value of $x$ will be
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
In circular motion with constant speed, magnitude of instantaneous velocity,& ${v}_{ins} = \omegar$.

Time taken to turn by~$90 °$~will be~$= \dfrac{\dfrac{π}{2}}{ω} = \dfrac{π}{2\omega}$.

Displacement will be equal to the length of $AB = \sqrt{r^{2} + r^{2}} = r\sqrt{2}$

Average velocity

${v}_{avg} = \dfrac{displacement}{time} = \dfrac{r\sqrt{2} \times 2\omega}{π} = \dfrac{2\sqrt{2}}{π}\omegar$

Hence, required ratio~$\dfrac{v\text{ins}}{v\text{avg}} = \dfrac{\omegar\pi}{2\sqrt{2}\omegar} = \dfrac{π}{2\sqrt{2}}$

Therefore,~$x = 2$.

questions.q: The angle of projection for a projectile to have same horizontal range and maximum height is :
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} & \frac{\mathrm{u}^2 \sin 2 \theta}{\mathrm{g}}=\frac{\mathrm{u}^2 \sin ^2 \theta}{2 \mathrm{~g}} \\ & 4 \sin \theta \cos \theta=\sin ^2 \theta \\ & 4=\tan \theta\end{aligned}$

questions.q: A disc is rolling without slipping on a surface. The radius of the disc is $R .$ At $t = 0,$ the top most point on the disc is $A$ as shown in figure. When the disc completes half of its rotation, the displacement of point $A$ from its initial position is
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
The displacement is the hypotenuse of the diameter and the distance travelled for half the rotation& $\piR$.

By using Pythagoras theorem,

Displacement of~$A = \sqrt{( 2R{)}^{2} + ( \piR{)}^{2}}$

$= R\sqrt{{π}^{2} + 4}$

questions.q: A projectile is launched at an angle $\alpha$~with the horizontal with a velocity $20\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm{ms}^{-1}$. After $10s$, its inclination with horizontal is $\beta$. The value of $tan\beta$ will be :  \left(g = 10{ms}^{- 2}\right)$.$
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Component of velocity in horizontal direction,

${v}_{x} = 20cos\alpha = {v}_{2}cos\beta$

Component of velocity in vertical direction,

${v}_{y} = 20sin\alpha - g \times 10 = {v}_{2}sin\beta$

$⇒ tan\beta = \dfrac{20sin\alpha - 100}{20cos\alpha}$

$⇒ tan\beta = tan\alpha - \dfrac{5}{cos\alpha}$

$⇒ tan\beta = tan\alpha - 5sec\alpha$

questions.q: A player kicks a football with an initial speed of $25\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm{ms}^{-1}$ at an angle of $45 °$ from the ground. What are the maximum height and the time taken by the football to reach at the highest point during motion? (Take $g = 10{ms}^{- 2}$)
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
$\theta = 45 °$

$H = \dfrac{u^{2}\sin^{2}\theta}{2g} = \dfrac{( 25{)}^{2} \times \left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right)}{2 \times 10} = \dfrac{125}{8}\text{m}$

and time $t = \dfrac{T}{2}$

$= \dfrac{usin\theta}{g} = \dfrac{25\left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right)}{10} = \dfrac{25}{10\sqrt{2}} = \dfrac{5}{2\sqrt{2}}\text{s}$

questions.q:
A body of mass $10$ kg is projected at an angle of $45 °$ with the horizontal. The trajectory of the body is observed to pass through a point \left(20, 10\right)$. If $T$ is the time of flight, then its momentum vector, at time $t = \dfrac{T}{2}$, is _____ .
[Take $g = 10ms^{- 2}$]$
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
It is given that the projectile passes through& \left(20, 10\right)$~and angle of projection is~$\theta = 45 °$. Using the trajectory equation,

$y = xtan\theta - \dfrac{gx^{2}}{2u^{2}\cos^{2}\theta}$

$⇒ 10 = 20 - \dfrac{\left(10\right)\left(100\right)}{u2}$

$⇒ u = 20ms^{- 1}$

Now the time of flight of projectile,

$T = \dfrac{2usin\theta}{g}$

$⇒ T = \dfrac{\left(2\right)\left(20\right)}{\sqrt{2}\left(10\right)} = 2\sqrt{2}s ⇒ \dfrac{T}{2} = 2s$

Now velocity of the projectile at any time~$t$~can be written as,

$\overset{→}{v} = ucos\theta\overset{^}{i} + \left(usin\theta - gt\right)\overset{^}{j}$

$⇒ \overset{→}{v} = 10\sqrt{2}\overset{^}{i} + ( 10\sqrt{2} - 10\left(2\right) ] \overset{^}{j}ms^{- 1}$

Therefore, momentum $\overset{→}{p} = M\overset{→}{v} = 100\sqrt{2}\overset{^}{i} + \left(100\sqrt{2} - 200\right)\overset{^}{j}Ns$

$

questions.q: Two guns $A$ and $B$ can fire bullets at speeds $1km / s$ and $2km / s$ respectively. From a point on a horizontal ground, they are fired in all possible directions. The ratio of maximum areas covered by the bullets fired by the two guns, on the ground is:
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
$\dfrac{{A}_{1}}{{A}_{2}} = \dfrac{\pi{\left({R}_\max\right)}_{1}^{2}}{\pi{\left({R}_\max\right)}_{2}^{2}} = \dfrac{{u}_{1}^{4}}{{u}_{2}^{4}} = \dfrac{1}{16}$

\left[∵ max . Range = \dfrac{u^{2}}{g}\right]$$

questions.q: Two balls with same mass and initial velocity, are projected at different angles in such a way that maximum height reached by first ball is 8 times higher than that of the second ball. $T_1$ and $T_2$ are the total flying times of first and second ball, respectively, then the ratio of $T_1$ and $T_2$ is :
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} & \text { Given, }\left(\mathrm{H}_{\max }\right)_1=8 \times\left(\mathrm{H}_{\max }\right)_2 \\ & \frac{\mathrm{u}^2 \sin ^2 \theta_1}{2 \mathrm{~g}}=8 \times \frac{\mathrm{u}^2 \sin ^2 \theta_2}{2 \mathrm{~g}} \\ & \Rightarrow \sin \theta_1=2 \sqrt{2} \sin \theta_2 \\ & \frac{\mathrm{~T}_1}{\mathrm{~T}_2}=\frac{2 \mathrm{u} \sin \theta_1 / \mathrm{g}}{2 \mathrm{u} \sin \theta_2 / \mathrm{g}}=\frac{\sin \theta_1}{\sin \theta_2}=2 \sqrt{2}\end{aligned}$

questions.q: A body is projected at $t=0$ with a velocity $10 \mathrm{~ms}^{-1}$ at an angle of $60^{{}^{{}^{\circ}}}$ with the horizontal. The radius of curvature of its trajectory at $t=1$ s is $R$. Neglecting air resistance and taking acceleration due to gravity $\mathrm{g}=10 \mathrm{~ms}^{-2}$, the value of $R$ is:
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution: Horizontal component of velocity $\mathrm{v}_{x}=10 \cos 60^{{}^{{}^{\circ}}}=5 \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s}$ vertical component of velocity $v_{y}=10 \cos 30^{{}^{{}^{\circ}}}=5 \sqrt{3} \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s}$ After $\mathrm{t}=1 \mathrm\sec$ Horizontal component of velocity $\mathrm{v}_{x}=5 \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s}$ Vertical component of velocity $v_{y}=|(5 \sqrt{3}-10)| \mathrm{m} / \mathrm{s}=10-5 \sqrt{3}$ Centripetal, acceleration $\mathrm{a}_{\mathrm{n}}=\frac{\mathrmv^{2}}{\mathrm{R}}\Rightarrow \mathrm{R}=\frac{\mathrm{v}_{\mathrm{x}}^{2}+\mathrm{v}_{\mathrm{y}}^{2}}{\mathrm{a}_{\mathrm{n}}}=\frac{25+100+75-100 \sqrt{3}}{10 \cos \theta}$ From figure (using (i)) $\tan \theta=\frac{10-5 \sqrt{3}}{5}=2-\sqrt{3} \Rightarrow \theta=15^{{}^{{}^{\circ}}}\mathrm{R}=\frac{100(2-\sqrt{3})}{10 \cos 15}=2.8 \mathrm{~m}$

questions.q: The initial speed of a projectile fired from ground is $u$. At the highest point during its motion, the speed of projectile is $\dfrac{3}{2}u$. The time of flight of the projectile is:
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
At maximum height, only horizontal velocity of the particle remains. Let the angle of project be& $\theta$. The horizontal velocity of the particle will remain same, therefore

$ucos\theta = \dfrac{\sqrt{3}u}{2} ⇒ \theta = 30 °$

Now, time of flight of projectile is

$T = \dfrac{2usin\theta}{g} = \dfrac{u}{g}$

questions.q: A particle of mass $m$ projected with a velocity $u$ making an angle of $30 °$ with the horizontal. The magnitude of angular momentum of the projectile about the point of projection when the particle is at its maximum height $h$ is :
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Angular momentum at maximum height will be, $L = \left(mucos\theta\right)h$, where $h =$maximum height

Therefore, $L = mucos\theta \times \dfrac{u^{2}\sin^{2}\theta}{2g}$

$= \dfrac{mu^{3}}{2g} \times \dfrac{3}{2} \times \left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right)2 = \dfrac{\sqrt{3}mu^{3}}{16g}$

questions.q: A projectile is projected with velocity of $25ms^{- 1}$ at an angle $\theta$ with the horizontal. After $t$ seconds its inclination with horizontal becomes zero. If $R$ represents horizontal range of the projectile, the value of $\theta$ will be : [use $useg = 10ms^{- 2}$]
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
From the information given in the question, after time& $t$~the inclination of the projectile becomes zero i.e. the projectile is at the highest point. Therefore,

$t = \dfrac{T}{2} = \dfrac{usin\theta}{g}$.

The rang of the projectile~$R = \dfrac{2u^{2}sin\theta cos\theta}{g}$.

Now,

$\dfrac{R}{t2} = \dfrac{2u^{2}sin\theta cos\theta}{g} \times \dfrac{g2}{u^{2}\sin^{2}\theta} ==2gcot\theta$⇒ $\theta = \cot^{- 1} \left(\dfrac{R}{20t^{2}}\right)

$

questions.q: The trajectory of a projectile near the surface of the earth is given as $y = 2x - 9x^{2} .$ If it were launched at an angle ${\theta}_{0}$ with speed ${v}_{0}$ then \left(g = 10{ms}^{- 2}\right):
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
y = 2x - 9x^{2}$
Comparing above equation with general equation of trajectory of projectile $y = xtan \theta \left($1 - $\dfrac{x}{R}\right)
$tan$\theta =$2$
$⇒ sin$\theta = \dfrac{2}{\sqrt{5}} or $cos$\theta = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{5}}
\theta = \sin^{- 1} \left(\dfrac{2}{\sqrt{5}}\right)or \theta = \cos^{- 1} \left(\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{5}})
And R = 2/9
$R = $\dfrac{{v0}^{2}\sin 2\theta}{g} = \dfrac{2}{9}
After substituting the value for g and \sin 2θ. We get ${v}_{0} = \dfrac{3}{5}$m/s$$

questions.q: Two bodies are projected from ground with same speeds $40ms^{- 1}$ at two different angles with respect to horizontal. The bodies were found to have same range. If one of the body was projected at an angle of $60 °$, with horizontal then sum of the maximum heights, attained by the two projectiles, is _____~$m$. (Given~$g = 10ms^{- 2}$)
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
For two projectiles with same speed to have the same horizontal range, angle of projection will be& ${θ}_{1} + {θ}_{2} = 90 °$.

Therefore,~${θ}_{2} = 90 ° - 60 ° = 30 °$.

Now, required sum of maximum heights will be,

\left({H}_\max\right)1 + \left({H}_\max\right)2 = \dfrac{u^{2}\sin^{2}{θ}_{1}}{2g} + \dfrac{u^{2}\sin^{2}{θ}_{2}}{2g}$

$= \dfrac{402}{20}\left(\dfrac{1}{4} + \dfrac{3}{4}\right) = 80m$

$

questions.q:
The projectile motion of a particle of mass $5g$ is shown in the figure.

The initial velocity of the particle is~$5\sqrt{2}\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm{ms}^{-1}$ and the air resistance is assumed to~be negligible. The magnitude of the change in~momentum between the points $A$~and $B$ is~$x \times {10}^{- 2}{kgms}^{- 1}$. The value of $x$,& to the nearest& integer, is ___ .
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
$| \overset{→}{u} | = | \overset{→}{v} |$

$\overset{→}{u} = ucos45\overset{^}{i} + usin45\overset{^}{j}$

$\overset{→}{v} = vcos45\overset{^}{i} - vsin45\overset{^}{j}$

$| \overset{→}{\Delta P} | = \left|m\left(\overset{→}{v} - \overset{→}{u}\right)\right|$

$\Delta P = 2musin45 °= 2 \times 5 \times {10}^{- 3} \times 5\sqrt{2} \times \dfrac{1}{2}$

$\Delta P = 50 \times {10}^{- 3}= 5 \times {10}^{- 2}$.

questions.q:
A particle is projected at an angle of $30^{{}^{{}^{\circ}}}$ from horizontal at a speed of $60 \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s}$. The height traversed by the particle in the first second is $\mathrm{h}_0$ and height traversed in the last second, before it reaches the maximum height, is $h_1$. The ratio $h_0: h_1$ is _________
[Take, $\mathrm{g}=10 \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s}^2$ ]
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} & \mathrm{S}_1=30 \times 1-\frac{1}{2} \times 10 \times 1=25 \\ & \mathrm{~S}_3=30+\left(\frac{-10}{2}\right) \times(2 \times 3-1)=5 \\ & \frac{\mathrm{~S}_1}{\mathrm{~S}_3}=\frac{25}{5}=5\end{aligned}$

questions.q: A body starts falling freely from height $H$ hits an inclined plane in its path at height $h$. As a result of this perfectly elastic impact, the direction of the velocity of the body becomes horizontal. The value of $\dfrac{H}{h}$ for which the body will take the maximum time to reach the ground is _____.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Total time of flight $= T$ can be written as,

$T = \sqrt{\dfrac{2h}{g}} + \sqrt{\dfrac{2\left(H - h\right)}{g}}$

For maximum time $= \dfrac{dT}{dh} = 0$

$⇒ \sqrt{\dfrac{2}{g}}\left(\dfrac{1}{2\sqrt{h}} - \dfrac{1}{2\sqrt{H - h}}\right) = 0$

$⇒ \sqrt{H - h} = \sqrt{h}$

$⇒ h = \dfrac{H}{2} ⇒ \dfrac{H}{h} = 2$

questions.q: An object is projected in the air with initial velocity $u$ at an angle $\theta$. The projectile motion is such that the horizontal range $R$, is maximum. Another object is projected in the air with a horizontal range half of the range of first object. The initial velocity remains same in both the case. The value of the angle of projection, at which the second object is projected, will be _____& degree.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
The maximum range is given by,& ${R}_\max = \dfrac{u^{2}\sin 2\left(45 °\right)}{g} = \dfrac{u2}{g}$.

For the range to be half of the maximum range,

$\dfrac{Rmax}{2} = \dfrac{u2}{2g} = \dfrac{u^{2}\sin 2\theta}{g}$

$⇒ \sin 2\theta = \dfrac{1}{2}$

$⇒ 2\theta = 30 ° \text{or}2\theta = 150 °$

$⇒ \theta = 15 ° , 75 °$

Therefore, answer is~$15\text{or}75$
